verdict.rationale: NotebookLM lets users interact via natural-language chat to query sources, request custom conversational styles/roles, and ask questions (notebooklm-docs-2, notebooklm-docs-7, notebooklm-docs-28), which is a genuine natural-language interface. However, many core actions (uploading sources, converting notes, generating mind maps/slide decks/audio overviews) are triggered via UI menus/buttons rather than free-form commands, and community feedback notes limits like being unable to have it search for and incorporate new sources on its own (notebooklm-comm-4). Missing for 10: evidence of natural-language commands driving broader agentic actions (e.g., source discovery, format generation, sharing) rather than just chat Q&A and style prompts, and independent confirmation of command robustness.
